newsitem.title: USA: Plains fed cattle market mostly $72.00 - feedlot.
newsitem.headline: Plains fed cattle market mostly $72.00 - feedlot.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade Thursday was light to moderate at prices mostly unchanged from early-week sales in Kansas and the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area, feedlot sources said.

About 6,500 head traded in the Panhandle at $72.00 per cwt, with one pen of select to mostly choice graded steers at $72.50, USDA and private sources said. USDA reported 70,800 head sold in that area for the week as of Thursday afternoon.
An estimated 1,800 head sold in Kansas at $72.00, with the week to date estimated at 84,400, according to USDA.
Sales in Nebraska this week were mostly at $73.00 to $74.00, with an extreme top at $75.00 paid on some cattle delivered to plants, USDA confirmed.
Showlists at Plains feedlots were mostly depleted this week, and those cattle left over had 100 days or less on feed, cattle feeders said.
Fed cattle prices were supported by tight supplies of choice graded cattle and strong beef demand, sources said.
Prices on choice-grading beef have jumped in recent days, due to tight supplies of well-fed cattle, sources noted.
USDA quoted cutout values on choice, yield-grade 3 beef carcasses weighing 550 to 700 lbs at $118.53 per cwt Thursday, up $4.40 since Wednesday last week.
